theme_zh: 公司要搬辦公室：在會議中提出建議
summary_zh: 學會在討論搬辦公室的會議上，用 Why don't we… / I'd suggest that… 有禮貌地提出建議，並比較不同選項的優缺點。

vocab.definition: a small list of the best options, chosen from a longer list, before the final decision
vocab.example: We've got three candidates on the shortlist for the job.
vocab.example_zh: 這個職缺我們有三位候選人進入最後名單。

vocab.definition: the trip you make to get to work and back home every day
vocab.example: My commute takes about forty minutes by train.
vocab.example_zh: 我搭火車通勤大約要四十分鐘。

vocab.zh: 開放式的（沒有隔間的辦公空間）
vocab.definition: describing an office with one large shared space instead of separate rooms (Americans also say "open office")
vocab.example: Open-plan offices feel bright, but they can be noisy.
vocab.example_zh: 開放式辦公室感覺很明亮，但可能會很吵。

vocab.zh: 共用座位制（不固定座位）
vocab.definition: a system where workers don't have their own desk and use whichever one is free
vocab.example: With hot-desking, you have to clear your desk at the end of every day.
vocab.example_zh: 採用共用座位制的話，每天下班都要把桌面清空。

vocab.definition: to think carefully about the good and bad points of something before deciding
vocab.example: Take some time to weigh the pros and cons before you reply.
vocab.example_zh: 回覆之前，花點時間好好權衡一下優缺點。

vocab.zh: 取捨、權衡（得到一樣就要犧牲另一樣）
vocab.definition: a situation where you accept something bad in order to get something good
vocab.example: A bigger office means higher rent. That's the trade-off.
vocab.example_zh: 辦公室大一點，租金就比較貴，這就是取捨。

vocab.definition: agreeing with and supporting a plan or idea
vocab.example: Is everyone on board with the new schedule?
vocab.example_zh: 大家都同意新的時程嗎？

vocab.zh: （把想法）先給某人看看、問問意見
vocab.definition: to run something by someone: to tell someone about an idea or plan to get their opinion or approval
vocab.example: Let me run this design by the legal team before it goes out.
vocab.example_zh: 這份設計發出去之前，我先拿給法務看一下。

reading.title: Where Should We Move?
paragraphs: Our office lease ends next June, and the landlord has told us the rent is going up by almost 30%. Instead of simply renewing the lease, the management team has decided to look at other options, and they'd like your input before anything is final.

We've drawn up a shortlist of three places. The first is a smaller space in our current building, which would mean no change to anyone's commute. The second is a bright open-plan space near the train station. It's bigger, but the rent is higher. The third is the cheapest option: a shared office downtown, where we would switch to hot-desking, since most of us are only in the office two or three days a week.

Each option comes with a trade-off. Staying where we are is easy, but we'd lose two meeting rooms. The office near the station is great for anyone who comes in by train, but it would eat into our budget. Hot-desking saves money, but some people really like having their own desk. And whichever place we choose, we'll have to pay a new security deposit, so we need to plan for that, too.

Why don't you take a few minutes to weigh the options and tell us what matters most to you? We'll run your answers by the managers next Friday. A move only works if everyone is on board, so please be honest.

questions.q: Why is the company thinking about moving?
options: The office is too small for the team
The rent is going up by almost 30%
The landlord is selling the building
Most people want to work from home
questions.explain_zh: 第一段：「the landlord has told us the rent is going up by almost 30%.」房東說租金要漲將近三成。

questions.q: Which option would not change anyone's commute?
options: The open-plan space near the train station
The shared office downtown
A smaller space in the current building
None of them
questions.explain_zh: 第二段：「a smaller space in our current building, which would mean no change to anyone's commute.」留在同一棟大樓，通勤就不會改變。

questions.q: Why does the company most likely want to hear from staff before deciding?
options: Because the managers have already chosen the station office
Because the staff will have to pay the security deposit
Because the move will only succeed if people support it
Because the landlord asked for everyone's opinion
questions.explain_zh: 推論題：最後一段「A move only works if everyone is on board」——搬家要大家支持才會順利，所以公司先問員工意見。

grammar.point: Making suggestions: Why don't we… / I'd suggest that…
grammar.point_zh: 提出建議：Why don't we… / I'd suggest that…

guide.key_zh: Why don't we…? 是友善的提議，不是在問為什麼；正式一點用 I'd suggest…

uses.label_zh: 口語、友善的提議：我們要不要…？

uses.note_zh: 美式與正式英文：that 後面用原形，主詞是第三人稱也不加 s（英式常說 should + 原形）
口語也常說 How about we + 原形動詞？

mistakes.wrong: I suggest you to send it.
mistakes.why_zh: suggest 後面不接「人 + to V」

mistakes.wrong: Why we don't ask the team?
mistakes.right: Why don't we ask the team?
mistakes.why_zh: 這是問句，don't 要放在 we 前面

examples.en: Why don't we visit all three offices before we decide?
examples.zh: 我們要不要先去看過三個地點再決定？

examples.en: I'd suggest that we keep at least two meeting rooms.
examples.zh: 我建議我們至少保留兩間會議室。

examples.en: How about asking the team which days they usually come in?
examples.zh: 要不要問問大家通常哪幾天進辦公室？

exercises.q: ___ we visit all three places this week? (用 Why 開頭提出建議：我們要不要…？)
exercises.explain_zh: Why don't we + 原形動詞？是友善的提議，don't 要放在 we 前面（✗ Why we don't…?  ✗ Why not we…?）。Shall we…? / Should we…? / How about we…? 也能提出建議，但這題練的是 Why don't we。

exercises.q: I'd suggest that the team ___ the new office before we sign the lease.
options: visited
visit
to visit
visiting
exercises.explain_zh: I'd suggest that + 主詞 + 原形動詞：提出建議時，that 子句的動詞用原形，主詞是 the team 也不加 s，所以是 visit（美式與正式英文的標準用法；英式也常說 should visit）。不要因為有 I'd 就把動詞改成過去式 visited；suggest 不接 to visit，that 子句裡也不能只放 visiting。

options: I suggest you to choose the office near the station.
I'd suggest to choose the office near the station.
I'd suggest choosing the office near the station.
I suggest you choosing the office near the station.
exercises.explain_zh: suggest 後面接名詞、V-ing 或 that 子句（that 可省略：I'd suggest you choose…），不接 to V，也不接「人 + to V」或「人 + V-ing」。正確是 I'd suggest choosing…

exercises.q: What about ___ (stay) in this building and giving up two meeting rooms?
exercises.explain_zh: How about / What about 後面接 V-ing，所以是 staying（後面的 giving 也是 V-ing）。

exercises.q: A coworker suggests moving downtown, but you'd like to check the costs first. Which reply is correct and polite?
options: Why don't we compare the costs first?
No, that's a bad idea.
You should to compare the costs first.
Why we don't compare the costs first?
exercises.explain_zh: 用 Why don't we…? 提出另一個做法，語氣友善又不直接否定對方。「No, that's a bad idea.」文法沒錯但太直接、不禮貌；「You should to compare…」錯在 should 後面不加 to；「Why we don't…?」語序錯誤，應該是 Why don't we…?

listening.title: Choosing the new office

lines.speaker: A
lines.name: Jenny
lines.text: Okay, so we've got three offices on the shortlist. Kevin, which one do you like best?

lines.speaker: B
lines.name: Kevin
lines.text: Honestly, the one near the station. My commute would go from an hour to twenty minutes.

lines.speaker: A
lines.name: Jenny
lines.text: I know, but the rent is a lot higher. And the landlord wants a three-month security deposit.

lines.speaker: B
lines.name: Kevin
lines.text: Three months? That's a lot. Why don't we ask if they'd take two?

lines.speaker: A
lines.name: Jenny
lines.text: Good idea. I'd also suggest that we offer to sign a longer lease in return. Landlords usually like that.

lines.speaker: B
lines.name: Kevin
lines.text: Makes sense. What about hot-desking at the downtown place? Would people be on board with that?

lines.speaker: A
lines.name: Jenny
lines.text: Some would, but the design team really wants their own desks. That's the trade-off for the cheaper rent.

lines.speaker: B
lines.name: Kevin
lines.text: Then how about running a quick survey before Friday?

lines.speaker: A
lines.name: Jenny
lines.text: Perfect. I'll send it out this afternoon and run the results by the managers next week.

lines.speaker: B
lines.name: Kevin
lines.text: Great. Let me know if you need help going through the answers.

questions.q: Why does Kevin like the office near the station?
options: It's the cheapest option
His commute would be much shorter
It has the most meeting rooms
The landlord doesn't want a deposit
questions.explain_zh: Kevin 說：「My commute would go from an hour to twenty minutes.」通勤會從一小時縮短到二十分鐘。

questions.q: What does Jenny suggest offering the landlord?
options: A higher rent for the first year
Three months' deposit in cash
A longer lease in return for a smaller deposit
An earlier move-in date
questions.explain_zh: Kevin 提議問房東押金能不能只收兩個月，Jenny 接著說：「I'd also suggest that we offer to sign a longer lease in return.」用簽長一點的租約來交換較少的押金。

questions.q: Why might hot-desking be a problem at the downtown office?
options: The downtown office has no desks
Some people, like the design team, want their own desks
Kevin's commute would get longer
The survey showed that nobody likes it
questions.explain_zh: 推論題：Jenny 說「the design team really wants their own desks. That's the trade-off.」——省錢的代價是有些人不能有固定座位，所以不是每個人都會同意。

dictation: Why don't we ask if they'd take two?
I'd also suggest that we offer to sign a longer lease in return.
Then how about running a quick survey before Friday?

shadowing: Why don't we visit all three offices before we decide?
I'd suggest that we keep at least two meeting rooms.
Each option comes with a trade-off.
Let me run it by my manager first.

prompts.question: Your company is choosing a new office. Which is most important to you: a short commute, your own desk, or more meeting rooms? Make two suggestions.
prompts.question_zh: 公司在挑新辦公室。通勤短、有固定座位、還是會議室多，哪一個對你最重要？提出兩個建議。
hints: For me, the most important thing is…
prompts.sample: For me, the most important thing is a short commute, because I still come in three days a week. Why don't we choose the office near the station but take a smaller space there to save money? I'd also suggest that we set aside a few quiet rooms for phone calls, because open-plan offices can get really noisy.

prompts.question: A friend says, "I'm so bored. What should we do this weekend?" Make two or three suggestions.
prompts.question_zh: 朋友說：「好無聊喔，這個週末要做什麼？」提出兩三個建議。
prompts.sample: Why don't we try that new brunch place near the river on Saturday? After that, how about going for a walk if the weather's nice? And if it rains, we could just stay in and watch a movie.

writing.task: Your office manager has asked everyone which new office they prefer. Write a short reply (about 80–100 words): say which option you like and why, mention one trade-off, and make two suggestions.
writing.task_zh: 辦公室經理請大家說說想搬到哪個新辦公室。寫一則簡短回覆（約 80–100 字）：說你喜歡哪個選項、為什麼，提一個取捨，再提出兩個建議。
writing.sample: Hi Jenny, thanks for asking. I'd prefer the office near the train station, because it would cut my commute almost in half. I know the rent is higher, and that's the trade-off. Why don't we take a slightly smaller space there to keep the cost down? Most of us aren't in every day anyway. I'd also suggest that we set aside at least one quiet room for calls, since open-plan offices can get noisy. Happy to help with the survey if you need it. Best, Mimi
checklist_zh: 先說你喜歡哪一個選項和原因
用 trade-off 說明這個選項的取捨（得到什麼、要犧牲什麼）
用 Why don't we + 原形動詞 提出一個建議
用 I'd suggest that + 主詞 + 原形動詞 提出另一個建議

translation.zh: 我們要不要在簽租約之前，先去看看那間辦公室？
translation.en: Why don't we go and see the office before we sign the lease?
alt: Why don't we visit the office before we sign the lease?
Why don't we take a look at the office before signing the lease?
Why don't we go see the office before we sign the lease?

translation.zh: 我建議我們先比較這三個地點的租金。
translation.en: I'd suggest that we compare the rent at all three places first.
alt: I'd suggest comparing the rent at the three places first.
I'd suggest that we first compare the rent for the three locations.
Each option comes with a trade-off.
There's a trade-off with every option.

reading.title: The Office Move Nobody Wanted
paragraphs: When Hannah's company announced it was giving up its downtown office, most people had already seen the writing on the wall. The rent had nearly doubled since the last lease was signed, half the desks sat empty on Mondays and Fridays, and the finance team had been dropping hints for months. Still, knowing a move is coming and actually agreeing on where to go are two very different things.

Hannah was asked to run the planning meetings, and the first one was rough. The sales team wanted to stay central, close to their clients. The engineers, most of whom lived in the suburbs, were tired of long commutes. And almost everyone dug in their heels at the word "hot-desking." Within twenty minutes, the meeting had turned into a list of complaints.

Rather than defend any one option, Hannah changed the question. "Why don't we forget about the buildings for a second," she said, "and agree on what an office actually needs to do for us?" The answers were surprisingly similar: quiet space for focused work, rooms for client meetings, and a reason to come in at all. Once that list was on the whiteboard, the options started to sort themselves out.

The sticking point was still hot-desking. Hannah didn't try to force it through. Instead, she offered a compromise: "I'd suggest that each team keep a small zone of its own, with a few permanent desks for people who come in four or five days a week." It cost a little more, but it took the heat out of the discussion.

In the end, the company chose a smaller office halfway between the city center and the suburbs. Not everyone loved it, but nobody felt ignored, and the move went ahead without anyone dragging their feet. As Hannah put it afterward, people rarely need to get their way; they need to feel that their concerns were taken seriously.

questions.q: What does "most people had already seen the writing on the wall" suggest?
options: They were shocked by the announcement
They had expected a move for some time
They had read about the move in an email
They wanted to stay in the downtown office
questions.explain_zh: 推論題：see the writing on the wall 指「早就看出（壞事）要發生」。後面列出租金幾乎翻倍、空位多、財務部一直暗示，所以大家早有預感要搬。

questions.q: How did Hannah get the first meeting back on track?
options: She chose an office herself and announced it
She got everyone to agree on their needs first
She cancelled hot-desking completely
She let the sales team make the final decision
questions.explain_zh: 第三段：「Why don't we forget about the buildings for a second, and agree on what an office actually needs to do for us?」她先讓大家對需求有共識，而不是爭論哪棟大樓。

questions.q: Why did Hannah's compromise most likely "take the heat out of the discussion"?
options: It was the cheapest option
It let people who come in most days keep their own desk
It meant nobody had to come into the office anymore
It moved the office closer to the clients
questions.explain_zh: 推論題：大家最反對的是 hot-desking（sticking point），她讓常進辦公室的人保有固定座位，解決了最大的不滿，討論就不再那麼火爆。

listening.title: Hearing out the engineers

lines.speaker: A
lines.name: Hannah
lines.text: Raj, before you say anything — I know the engineers aren't thrilled about the new place.

lines.speaker: B
lines.name: Raj
lines.text: Not thrilled is putting it mildly. Half my team's already asking if they can work from home full-time.

lines.speaker: A
lines.name: Hannah
lines.text: Okay, fair. But hear me out. What if we—

lines.speaker: B
lines.name: Raj
lines.text: If it's hot-desking again, honestly, I'm not sure—

lines.speaker: A
lines.name: Hannah
lines.text: It's not. Well, not exactly. Why don't we give your team its own zone? Six permanent desks, by the windows.

lines.speaker: B
lines.name: Raj
lines.text: Six? There are nine of us.

lines.speaker: A
lines.name: Hannah
lines.text: Right, but only six come in most days. The other three are in once a week. They can use the shared desks.

lines.speaker: B
lines.name: Raj
lines.text: Hmm. That might fly. I'd still suggest that we run it past the team before anything's set in stone, though.

lines.speaker: A
lines.name: Hannah
lines.text: Absolutely. Can you sound them out this week?

lines.speaker: B
lines.name: Raj
lines.text: Sure, give me till Friday. And if they push back, can we meet halfway?

lines.speaker: A
lines.name: Hannah
lines.text: That's the whole idea. Nobody's getting steamrolled on this one.

questions.q: How do Raj's engineers feel about the new office?
options: They're excited about it
They're unhappy, and some want to work from home full-time
They don't care where the office is
They've already chosen their desks
questions.explain_zh: Raj 說「Not thrilled is putting it mildly」（說不太開心還算客氣了），而且「Half my team's already asking if they can work from home full-time.」

questions.q: Why does Hannah think six desks could be enough for a team of nine?
options: Only six come in most days, and the other three can use shared desks
Three of them are leaving the company
The other three will work in the sales zone
The office has extra desks by the windows
questions.explain_zh: Hannah 說：「only six come in most days. The other three are in once a week. They can use the shared desks.」常進辦公室的只有六個人，其他三人用共用座位就好。

questions.q: What does Raj mean when he says "That might fly"?
options: The idea is too risky
The idea might be accepted
The team will travel to the new office
He wants to decide very quickly
questions.explain_zh: 推論題：口語 something might fly 指「這個點子可能行得通、大家可能會接受」。他接著說要先問過團隊，表示態度轉為願意考慮。

dictation: Half my team's already asking if they can work from home full-time.
Why don't we give your team its own zone?
Can you sound them out this week?

glossary.definition: clear signs that something bad or unwelcome is going to happen

glossary.zh: 堅持不讓步（dig in one's heels 的過去式）
glossary.definition: refused to change their opinion or do what others wanted
an issue that stops people from reaching an agreement

glossary.zh: 拖拖拉拉、不情願地拖延
glossary.definition: doing something slowly because you don't really want to do it

glossary.zh: 探探（某人的）口風、先問問看法（sound someone out）
glossary.definition: to talk to people informally to find out what they think about a plan
